This guide explains the two ways to select a Stats NZ release:

1. let the package search the official release calendar, or
2. provide an explicit information-release URL for a reproducible historical
   read.

## Calendar discovery

`statsnz_latest_release()` searches release-calendar months from newest to
oldest, applies the release family's title rule, and returns the newest page
published on or before `as_of`.  Calendar discovery therefore needs network
access and can change as Stats NZ publishes new releases.

```{r calendar-live}
if (interactive()) {
  latest_cpi <- statsnzreleases::statsnz_latest_release(
    "nz_stats_cpi",
    as_of = Sys.Date(),
    lookback_months = 18L
  )
  latest_cpi
}
```

Use a smaller `lookback_months` when a workflow has a known publication window.
The argument is bounded by the package to prevent an unintentional unbounded
calendar search.  If no matching page is found, the package reports a typed
`statsnz_release_not_found` error after recording the first request failure in
the message when one is available.

## Explicit historical pages

For analysis that must be repeatable, record the exact page URL and pass it to
`read_statsnz_release()`.  The reader still validates that the page belongs to
the requested release family before selecting attachments.

```{r explicit-live}
if (interactive()) {
  historical_gdp <- statsnzreleases::read_statsnz_release(
    "nz_stats_gdp",
    release_url = paste0(
      "https://www.stats.govt.nz/information-releases/",
      "gross-domestic-product-march-2026-quarter/"
    ),
    series = "SNEA.SG00NAC00B15",
    start_period = "2020.03",
    end_period = "2025.12",
    quiet = FALSE
  )
  head(historical_gdp)
}
```

The period bounds are inclusive and accept annual (`YYYY`) or sub-annual
(`YYYY.MM`) values.  `series` matches exact Stats NZ series references.  The
result remains a `statsnz_release_data` tibble, so filtering does not discard
its release and attachment provenance.

## Files before data

When you need to inspect an information-release page before choosing a read,
use `statsnz_release_files()`.  It returns the attachment name, title,
extension, stated size, and official HTTPS URL.  This is also a useful first
diagnostic when a page has changed its attachment layout.

```{r files-live}
if (interactive()) {
  files <- statsnzreleases::statsnz_release_files(
    paste0(
      "https://www.stats.govt.nz/information-releases/",
      "gross-domestic-product-march-2026-quarter/"
    )
  )
  files[, c("name", "title", "extension", "url")]
}
```

## Cache and provenance

Attachments are cached below `statsnz_cache_dir()` using a URL fingerprint and
release family.  A cached non-empty file is reused unless `refresh = TRUE`.
For a reproducible project, either leave the default cache in place and record
its provenance or pass a project-managed cache directory explicitly:

```{r cache}
cache_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "statsnzreleases-example-cache")
basename(statsnzreleases::statsnz_cache_dir())
basename(cache_dir)
```

After a successful read, store the result of
`statsnz_provenance(data)` with the analysis outputs.  In addition to the page
URL and retrieval time, the attachment table records local paths, byte sizes,
and SHA-256 hashes, making it possible to detect a changed download.

## Network and credentials

Requests are restricted to official `https://www.stats.govt.nz` URLs and use a
bounded connect/request timeout.  The package does not require credentials or
perform installation-time downloads.  A populated cache can avoid
re-downloading an attachment once its page metadata has been retrieved, but
the reader still fetches the information-release page before selecting files.
For a fully offline demonstration, [Getting started](getting-started.html)
feeds an installed, attributed CPI snapshot through the same public reader and
parser path. See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.html) for typed errors and
offline checks.
